title: CRA I/II - Beijing/Shanghai/Guangzhou
description:
CRA I/II - Beijing/Shanghai/Guangzhou

Syneos Health® is a leading fully-integrated life sciences services organization built to accelerate customer success. We partner with innovators at every point across the drug development and commercialization continuum, helping them navigate complexity, anticipate change and accelerate progress.

Our Clinical Solutions team members act with a drug development mindset, applying their years of experience and deep expertise to truly understand customer needs and represent those in the solutions we shape.

Whether you join us in a Functional Service Provider partnership or a Full-Service environment, you’ll collaborate with passionate problem solvers, innovating as a team to help our customers achieve their goals. We are agile and driven to deliver – for one another, our customers, and, most importantly, for those in need.

Discover what your 25,000 future colleagues already know:

Why Syneos Health
• We are passionate about developing our people, through career development and progression; supportive and engaged line management; technical and therapeutic area training; peer recognition and total rewards program.
• We are committed to building an inclusive culture – where you can authentically be yourself. Central to this is our purpose – Driven to Deliver – which captures the passion of our colleagues to show up each day and shape solutions that have the ability to dramatically impact someone’s life.
• We are continuously building the company we all want to work for and our customers want to work with. Why? Because we know that when we bring together smart colleagues from across the world, we can shape the future of healthcare, driving impact for customers and defining the pace of patient progress.

Job Responsibilities

  • Performs site qualification, site initiation, interim monitoring, site management activities and close-out visits (performed on-site or remotely) ensuring regulatory, ICH-GCP and/or Good Pharmacoepidemiology Practice (GPP) and protocol compliance. Uses judgment and experience to evaluate overall performance of site and site staff and to provide recommendations regarding site-specific actions; immediately communicates/escalates serious issues to the project team and develops action plans. Maintains a working knowledge of ICH/GCP Guidelines or other applicable guidance, relevant regulations, and company SOPs/processes.
  • Verifies the process of obtaining informed consent has been adequately performed and documented for each subject/patient, as required/appropriate. Demonstrates diligence in protecting the confidentiality of each subject/patient. Assesses factors that might affect subject/patient’s safety and clinical data integrity at an investigator/physician site such as protocol deviation/violations and pharmacovigilance issues.
  • Per the Clinical Monitoring/Site Management Plan (CMP/SMP): Assesses site processes. Conducts Source Document Review of appropriate site source documents and medical records. Verifies required clinical data entered in the case report form (CRF) is accurate and complete. Applies query resolution techniques remotely and on site, and provides guidance to site staff as necessary, driving query resolution to closure within agreed timelines. Utilizes available hardware and software to support the effective conduct of the clinical study data review and capture. Verifies site compliance with electronic data capture requirements.
  • May perform investigational product (IP) inventory, reconciliation and reviews storage and security. Verifies the IP has been dispensed and administered to subjects/patients according to the protocol. Verifies issues or risks associated with blinded or randomized information related to IP. Applies knowledge of GCP/local regulations and organizational procedures to ensure IP is appropriately (re)labelled, imported and released/returned.
  • Routinely reviews the Investigator Site File (ISF) for accuracy, timeliness and completeness. Reconciles contents of the ISF with the Trial Master File (TMF). Ensures the investigator/physician site is aware of the requirement of archiving essential documents in accordance with local guidelines and regulations.
  • Documents activities via confirmation letters, follow-up letters, trip reports, communication logs, and other required project documents as per SOPs and Clinical Monitoring Plan/Site Management Plan. Supports subject/patient recruitment, retention and awareness strategies. Enters data into tracking systems as required to track all observations, ongoing status and assigned action items to resolution.
  • For assigned activities, understands project scope, budgets, and timelines; manages site-level activities / communication to ensure project objectives, deliverables and timelines are met. Must be able to quickly adapt to changing priorities to achieve goals / targets.
  • May act as primary liaison with study site personnel, or in collaboration with Central Monitoring Associate. Ensures all assigned sites and project-specific site team members are trained and compliant with applicable requirements
  • Prepares for and attends Investigator Meetings and/or sponsor face to face meetings. Participates in global clinical monitoring/project staff meetings (inclusive of Sponsor representation, as applicable) and attends clinical training sessions according to the project specific requirements.
  • Provides guidance at the site and project level towards audit readiness standards and supports preparation for audit and required follow-up actions.
  • Maintains a working knowledge of ICH/GCP Guidelines or other applicable guidance, relevant regulations, and company SOPs/processes; completes assigned training as required. For Real World Late Phase, the CRA II will use the business card title of Site Management Associate II. Additional responsibilities include:Site support throughout the study lifecycle from site identification through close-out. Knowledge of local requirements for real world late phase study designs.Chart abstraction activities and data collection
    Collaboration with Sponsor affiliates, medical science liaisons and local country staff. The SMA II may be requested to train junior staff. Identify and communicate out of scope activities to Lead CRA/Project Manager. Proactively suggest potential sites based on local knowledge of treatment patterns, patient advocacy and Health Care Provider (HCP) associations.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or RN in a related field or equivalent combination of education, training and experience
  • Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice/ICH Guidelines and other applicable regulatory requirements
  • Must demonstrate good computer skills and be able to embrace new technologies
  • Excellent communication, presentation and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to manage required travel of up to 75% on a regular basis
  • US ONLY: As part of your employment with Syneos Health, you may be deployed to Sites that require certain medical and other personal information to gain facility access. Pursuant to our Employee Privacy Notice, Syneos Health can provide the Sites with the information necessary for you to gain such access. Further, a Site may ask you for additional information beyond that which Syneos Health has in its possession. You are required to comply with any such Site requests as a condition of your employment with Syneos Health. Please note that failure to provide requested information may result in a Site barring you from entry, which could put your ongoing employment at risk.

Over the past 5 years, we have worked with 94% of all Novel FDA Approved Drugs, 95% of EMA Authorized Products and over 200 Studies across 73,000 Sites and 675,000+ Trial patients.

title: Design Lead
description:
Design Lead

Westminster University


Supervisor: Director of Marketing

Department: Office of Marketing, Communication, and Events


Position Summary

The Design Lead is Westminster's visual brand steward, reporting to the Director of Marketing. This role moves beyond brand maintenance into proactively shaping where Westminster's brand goes next, bringing initiative, strategic vision, and hands-on craft to every project.

Reporting to the Director of Marketing and in partnership with the Junior Graphic Designer, the Design Lead originates creative concepts and campaign thinking, translates institutional strategy into compelling visual solutions, and actively problem-solves to elevate the brand across print, digital, social, advertising, and editorial materials. They work cross-functionally with the internal MarComm team and campus partners.

The ideal candidate pairs strong design execution with strategic, big-picture thinking: someone who is constantly asking how Westminster's brand can be stronger, more cohesive, and more distinctive. They're excited to bring that thinking to a mission-driven institution with a strong sense of community and a real commitment to educational values, and they're energized by the cultural and creative life around them.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

CREATIVE DIRECTION AND BRAND

  • Serve as vision holder for Westminster's brand, proactively identifying opportunities to strengthen and evolve the university's visual identity, and contributing creative concepts and strategic design solutions that advance university goals and elevate projects from concept through execution
  • Develop wireframes and visual direction for campaign initiatives, partnering with the web team and other campus partners
  • Evaluate creative work across departments to identify where visual direction should shift, translating institutional priorities into cohesive visual communications
  • Ensure consistency, quality, and brand alignment across all marketing and communications materials, print through digital

BRAND OPERATIONS AND PROJECT MANAGEMENT

  • Participate in project intake with the Director of Marketing, bringing design-specific questions to define project goals and creative briefs
  • Manage individual design projects and deadlines to ensure high-quality, timely execution
  • Strategize, design, and produce the Westminster Review magazine, annual event invitations, and other institutional publications
  • Translate campaigns across mediums — platform specs, reformatting, ensuring one campaign holds together from print to web
  • Develop and maintain university-wide design templates (Canva, PowerPoint, and other branded resources)
  • Co-manage print production and vendor relationships (estimates, specs, timelines, delivery); support sourcing of freelance creatives and specialty vendors
  • Maintain Westminster's brand portal (CLC Brand Manager 360)
  • Present creative work and brand direction to stakeholders, advocating for strategic design
  • Solve production and creative challenges proactively
  • Stay current on design trends and production best practices


TEAM LEADERSHIP AND MENTORSHIP

  • Mentor the Junior Graphic Designer and student employees, fostering craft and creative growth; track the team's project pipeline with the Director of Marketing
  • Present creative work and brand direction to external stakeholders/clients and internal teams
  • Partner closely with the Director of Marketing as a strategic creative counterpart — helping shape direction, not just receiving it


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Graphic Design, Visual Communications, or related field
  • 7+ years of professional graphic design experience, including meaningful agency or client-facing time and demonstrated growth into higher-level creative ownership
  • Strong portfolio demonstrating brand identity and systems-level thinking — not just campaign execution — across print, digital, social, web, and editorial
  • Demonstrated experience developing wireframes or UX/interface design for websites or digital products
  • Familiarity with Canva and PowerPoint, to support campus clients effectively
  • Demonstrated experience presenting creative work to executive stakeholders and/or external clients, and navigating feedback with confidence
  • Proven ability to translate a campaign or brand across multiple channels while maintaining cohesion
  • Expert proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite and Figma; working proficiency in XD or similar
  • Exceptional written, verbal, and visual communication skills

Preferred Qualifications

  • Motion graphics or animation experience (After Effects, Premiere Pro, or similar)
  • Illustration skills, or experience writing briefs for and managing illustrators/specialty creatives
  • Experience in higher education or another complex, multi-stakeholder institutional environment
  • Mentorship experience
  • Editorial design experience for print publications (magazines, annual reports, or similar)
  • Familiarity with brand portal/DAM systems (e.g., CLC Brand Manager 360) or similar platforms

title: Vi søker butikkmedarbeider i nattevaktstilling

title: RF Test Technician
description:
SWISSto12 is one of the world’s fastest-growing aerospace companies, evolving from its pioneering use of 3D printing technologies for high-performance Radio Frequency (RF) products and applications to recently announcing the manufacture of entire geostationary telecom satellites, called HummingSat, that define a new category in space.

HummingSat is the world’s first commercial telecom GEO SmallSat developed in collaboration with the European Space Agency (ESA). Its uniquely compact size combined with highly capable telecom payloads allows telecommunications operators to deploy a cost-efficient, compact, and agile asset without sacrificing performance or security. HummingSat has been selected by Intelsat to build the I-45 satellite, by Inmarsat to build three I-8 satellites, and recently by Astrum Mobile to build the NEASTAR-1 satellite.

SWISSto12 is also a leading provider of Radio-Frequency (RF) products and sub-systems for satellite communication and remote sensing applications. The company’s patented 3D printing technologies and associated product designs are unique to deliver lightweight, compact, highly performing, and competitive RF products.

We are seeking a highly motivated RT test technicians (different seniority levels can be considered) to join our team to perform the testing of the advanced antennas, RF products and systems that SWISSto12 develops. This role requires passion for laboratory environment and activities.

Responsibilities

  • Test antennas, passive RF devices, active RF devices or RF assemblies using Vector Network Analyzers (or similar equipment such as well as laboratory support equipment), following test plans and/or test procedures
  1. Type of tests: S-parameters (insertion loss, return loss, VSWR), antenna patterns (in anechoic chamber), power measurements, etc.
  2. Frequency range: between 0.5 GHz and 100 GHz.
  3. Type of projects: either development (R&D) projects or production.
  4. Prepare or contribute to prepare test setups.
  5. Report issues to test managers, project managers or RF engineers.
  • Install antennas or RF units/systems on test fixtures in the company’s own RF test (according to the assembly drawings and/or 3D models from the PDM system).
  • Support SWISSto12 operations and R&D teams on activities that are peripheral to RF test.

Additional functions:
  • In addition to the test activities, and depending on your background and interests, you might also participate in:
    1. Document test activities and prepare test reports.
    2. Contribute to maintain laboratory equipment.
    3. Support failure and troubleshooting investigations, as well as root-cause analysis activities.
    4. Contribute to development of test scripts.
    5. Courses or trainings for advanced RF system test.
    6. Utilize environmental test equipment (thermal and thermal vacuum, EMC/EMI).

Requirements

  • The candidate must have: attention to detail, problem-solving mindset, technical curiosity, willingness to learn and team collaboration.
  • 3+ years proven experience in laboratory and production-test environment, including handling of electronic hardware.
    • Candidates with less than 3 years but with experience in RF laboratory are also invited to apply.
  • Having understanding of RF and/or experience with RF systems or RF units is an asset.
  • Understanding of ESD, quality, safety, and similar rules and procedures.
  • Language: fluent in French and/or English

Benefits

Further details to be shared by our recruitment team.

More about SWISSto12:

SWISSto12 has successfully established contracts with Intelsat, Inmarsat, Astrum Mobile and ESA for HummingSat as well as contracts for their RF product line in Europe, and the US with prominent partners and customers such as Thales, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, SES and the ESA. SWISSto12 is a spin off from the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne (EPFL), is privately owned and backed by prominent Swiss and European Investors. SWISSto12 is headquartered in Lausanne, Switzerland, and operates a US and European-subsidiariesy in Foster City California. The company is well funded for its near and mid-term developments and backed by a solid customer revenue stream.

title: CMI Analyst France & Strategic Projects
description:
JOB PURPOSE

France is one of Unilever’s strategically important Foods markets, with a strong brand portfolio including global brands such as Knorr and locally-led brands such as Amora and Maille.

This role exists to bring the voice of the consumer into key business decisions for France Foods, while helping the wider Foods Europe CMI team generate faster, smarter and more cost-effective consumer learning across Europe.

You will work closely with the France CMI Lead, taking ownership of agreed areas of the France Foods agenda and partnering with the business to turn consumer, market and category understanding into action. Alongside the France scope, you will support key Foods Europe strategic projects and help bring more consumer research in-house, using the right mix of research, analytics, agile approaches and emerging tools.

You’ll be part of a team that believes insight should not just explain what is happening, but help shape better decisions, stronger innovation and sustainable growth.

We believe in doing work that matters — for people and the planet. Because here, we don’t just hire for jobs. We invite you to be part of something bigger.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • ​​Partner with the France CMI Lead to deliver the France Foods insight agenda, with clear ownership of agreed categories, projects and business priorities (eg cooking staples portfolio such as Knorr bouillons, seasonings, sauces).

  • ​Act as the Consumer & Market Insights partner for your area of the France portfolio, bringing consumer, market and category understanding into innovation and growth decisions.

  • ​Lead consumer learning for local innovation projects, from identifying the key business and consumer questions through research design, execution and translation into recommendations.

  • ​Identify relevant consumer, category and market trends, connecting multiple sources of information to highlight opportunities and risks for the France Foods business.

  • ​Design and execute consumer research end-to-end, using the right combination of qualitative, quantitative, agile and emerging research approaches.

  • ​Support Foods Europe CMI teams in bringing more research in-house, helping deliver studies faster and more cost-effectively while maintaining high standards of consumer learning.

  • ​Translate research and data into simple, actionable insights and recommendations that influence business decisions.

  • ​Leverage AI, analytics and emerging insight tools to make consumer learning faster, smarter and more impactful.

  • ​Build strong relationships across CMI and multifunctional teams, collaborating effectively across both the France and European agendas.​

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • ​​Experience in Consumer & Market Insights, Market Research, Analytics, Marketing, Customer Strategy & Planning, Category Management or another relevant commercial discipline.

  • ​Strong analytical thinking and ability to turn complex information, data and research findings into clear insights, implications and business recommendations.

  • ​Genuine curiosity about consumers, people and culture, with a passion for understanding what drives behaviour.

  • ​Learning mindset and can-do attitude, with the curiosity to test new tools and approaches, openness to feedback, and ability to adjust your approach as you learn.

  • ​Strong project management skills, with a willingness to be hands-on in designing and executing research as well as interpreting the results.

  • ​Fluent in French and English.

​​

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • ​​Experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research methodologies.

  • ​Comfortable using analytical tools and dashboards, such as Excel, Power BI or similar platforms.

  • ​Interest in using AI, analytics and new research approaches to improve the speed, quality and efficiency of insight generation.​

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
  • Localisation : Rueil Malmaison -France

description:
The New School Archives and Special Collections is hiring Archives Assistants to help with routine administrative tasks. Open to matriculated graduate students only, this is an on-campus position starting in Fall 2026, with possible extension through the 2026-2027 academic year. Preference will be given to students in the early stages of their academic program.

  • Setting up for and assisting researchers during visits to the Archives Research Room.

  • Locating, retrieving, and re-shelving materials.

  • Entering file-level inventories into archival management systems and computer applications such as Microsoft Word or Excel.

  • Conducting basic research to assist archivists in identifying and describing archival materials.

  • Writing summaries of research findings and abstracts of biographical and historical information.

  • Answering phone calls.

  • Organizing and replenishing supplies to support daily operations.

  • Other tasks to assist the archivists, as assigned.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • Matriculated graduate student, with ability to maintain consistent schedule for the summer.

  • Prior office experience.

  • Demonstrated professionalism and strong work ethic.

  • Superior English written and oral communication skills.

  • Aptitude for following precise written and oral instructions and to complete detail-oriented work with precision.

  • Research skills and ability to summarize findings in writing with precision.

  • Ability to work independently, with minimal supervision.

  • Ability to evaluate and correct one’s own work, when needed.

  • Provide welcoming, friendly customer service to wide range of visitors internal and external to the university.

  • Physical ability and willingness to lift and carry boxes weighing up to 50 lbs.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Customer service experience.

  • Early career graduate student.

  • Interest in 20th century American history.

  • Interest in the history of The New School and its departments/programs.

  • Familiarity with Google Suite (Calendar, Gmail, Docs, Sheets, etc.) and Microsoft Office.

title: Regional Director- Africa
description:
ABOUT ISRAAID

IsraAID is an international non-governmental humanitarian aid organization with its HQ based in Israel. Since we were founded in 2001, our teams have worked in emergency and long-term development settings in more than 60 countries around the world. IsraAID responds to emergencies and helps communities affected by crises rebuild their lives, and their futures, together. From hurricanes to refugee crises to global pandemics, we mobilize quickly and collaborate with communities at the deepest level, accompanying the process of becoming self-reliant in the ability to prepare and respond to emergencies and crises and return to adaptive functioning.

IsraAID has operated in Africa since 2011. The Africa Regional Desk currently oversees Country Offices in Kenya, Malawi, Uganda, and South Sudan, with programmes grounded in community resilience framework and tailored to some of the world's most complex humanitarian and development contexts.

ABOUT THE POSITION

The Director of Africa Region is the primary regional authority for IsraAID's Africa portfolio.. The Director is IsraAid’s regional representative and holds full line management and responsibility for Country Directors across the Africa region, operating with expanded authority and independence within the organization.

Working in close partnership with the Senior Director RRP and the Senior Management Team the Director of Africa Region leads the regional desk team (including the SPO for Africa Region), drives performance of Country Offices, and serves as the primary management interface between HQ departments and Country Directors in Malawi, Uganda, Kenya, and South Sudan. In addition, the Director of Africa Region is the key authority to lead the Regional Team in achieving the region’s objectives and deliverables through a matrix structure management lines. While officially part of the HQ team, the director if region leads the regional’s team collaboration across support functions ensuring that operational needs on the ground are sufficiently supported and implemented in line with organizational policies and practices.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

  1. Line Management & People Leadership
  • Hold formal line management responsibility for all Africa Region Country Directors (CDs) and the Senior Programme Officer (SPO), Africa Region, including setting performance expectations, defining objectives, and conducting performance reviews.
  • Provide ongoing guidance, mentoring, coaching, and advisory support to CDs, fostering leadership development and building future organizational capacity within the region.
  • Ensure CDs have clear direction and aligned workplans, and that leadership gaps or transitions are addressed proactively and with appropriate organizational support.
  • Lead and coordinate the Africa regional desk team under the matrix management structure, ensuring team members are well informed, prioritized, and coordinated.
  • Lead the region’s engagement at HQ and with departmental leaders, representing the countries in strategic conversations ensuring realities on the ground are considered and inform organizational decision making.
  • Represent the Africa region and IsraAid across external fora, with partners and in front of stakeholders.
  1. Country Office Performance, Risk & Stabilization
  • Hold primary accountability for the overall performance, stability, and risk profile of all Africa Country Offices, including oversight of strategic delivery and leadership effectiveness.
  • Ensure early identification of operational, financial, reputational, and contextual risks; mandate and oversee performance improvement or stabilization plans for underperforming or high-risk offices.
  • Provide decisive leadership during periods of crisis, transition, or CO instability — serving as the management anchor for complex situations that require direct intervention.
  1. Strategic Execution & Programme Quality
  • Guide the development and review of country strategies and annual workplans, ensuring coherence with IsraAID's global strategy, organizational standards, and resilience framework.
  • Ensure global programmatic quality standards are integrated throughout the CO programmatic portfolio across the region, working in close partnership with the Director of the Technical Unit and other relevant departments.
  • Collaborate across programmes to integrate resilience thinking, sustainability, and cross-cutting considerations (including MEAL, safeguarding, and inclusion) into programme design and delivery.
  • Ensure that learning, evidence, and adaptation systematically inform both programme delivery and strategic decision-making at CO, regional and HQ level.
  1. HQ Coordination & Regional Team Management
  • Serve as the primary lead of the Africa regional team under the matrix management structure, ensuring coherent, prioritized, and timely HQ support to Country Offices.
  • Coordinate with HQ technical, operational, and enabling functions to ensure guidance to COs is consistent, non-duplicative, and aligned with CO priorities and capacity.
  • Prevent CO overload through active prioritization of HQ requests and timelines; ensure competing demands are escalated and resolved at the appropriate level.
  • Ensure SPO Africa Region is well-supported, empowered, and proactively managing administrative and programmatic processes.
  1. Partnerships, Fundraising & Local Donor Engagement
  • Through guidance and in coordination with DevComs, support Country Directors in the cultivation of strategic partnerships, funding relationships, and donor engagement at the country level, ensuring coherence with organizational fundraising priorities.
  • Maintain and strengthen institutional relationships with key regional and country-level partners, coordinating introductions and handovers to preserve institutional continuity and trust.
  • Lead IsraAid’s regional positioning, donor engagement in Africa and identification of strategic funding opportunities under the guidance of the Senior Director RRP and in close collaboration with DevComs and IsraAids strategic offices..
  1. Safeguarding & Organizational Values
  • Champion and uphold IsraAID's safeguarding standards across all levels of the Africa portfolio, ensuring COs maintain a safe working environment and operate in accordance with organizational policies.
  • Ensure Country Directors and regional team members are appropriately trained, supported, and equipped to identify, report, and respond to safeguarding concerns.
  • Act as a senior organizational representative for accountability, ethical conduct, and compliance with IsraAID's values: Professionalism, Humanity, Collaboration, Flexibility, and Adaptability.

SCOPE & CONTEXT: NEW ROLE EXPECTATIONS

Success in 2026 will be measured by: stabilization of existing Country Offices; effective transition of CDs to the new regional structure; improved programmatic management and documentation; and a reduction in high-risk escalations requiring Senior Director intervention.

ESSENTIAL SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & COMPETENCIES

Education

  • Master's degree (or equivalent) in International Development, Project Management, Social Sciences, Humanitarian Affairs, or a related field relevant to IsraAID's work.

Experience

  • Minimum 10 years of progressive leadership and management experience in humanitarian and/or development settings at international level, including at least 5 years working in sub-Saharan Africa (required).
  • Proven track record of direct line management of Country Directors or equivalent senior managers across multiple countries or contexts.
  • Demonstrated experience in country office oversight, risk management, and performance management in fragile or complex operating environments.
  • Strong background in programme quality oversight across multiple sectors (Education, Health & Nutrition, Protection, WASH), with solid understanding of results-based management and resilience approaches.
  • Proven experience in financial management and oversight of significant multi-country budgets.
  • Experience in donor engagement and resource mobilization, including with institutional donors (UN agencies, private foundations, bilateral donors).
  • Experience managing matrix structures and coordinating multi-disciplinary HQ support teams.

Leadership & Management Competencies

  • Exceptional people leadership and line management skills — able to hold accountability while coaching, mentoring, and developing others.
  • Strong crisis management and stabilization capabilities; able to provide decisive leadership under pressure and ambiguity.
  • Proven ability to manage complex, multi-stakeholder environments and align diverse teams towards common goals.
  • High level of independence, initiative, and sound judgment; able to operate with limited direct oversight and make decisions at appropriate thresholds.
  • Strong organizational skills and track record of managing competing priorities and deadlines.

Technical & Programme Skills

  • Deep understanding of programme design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation, and learning processes in humanitarian and resilience contexts.
  • Familiarity with IASC guidelines and international humanitarian coordination structures.
  • Strong analytical skills and experience leading strategic planning processes.
  • Understanding of safeguarding principles, organizational compliance frameworks, and ethical standards in humanitarian organizations.

Interpersonal & Communication Skills

  • Highly developed interpersonal, communication, and negotiation skills — including the ability to influence, coach, and manage from varied roles and levels of authority.
  • Demonstrated cultural competency and ability to work effectively across diverse contexts, nationalities, and organizational cultures.
  • Commitment to IsraAID's organizational values: Professionalism, Humanity, Collaboration, Flexibility, and Adaptability.

IT & Languages

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and collaboration platforms (Teams, Zoom).
  • Fluency in English (required). Knowledge of French or other regional languages is an advantage.
  • Ability to travel to Africa Country Offices and IsraAID HQ on short notice.

ETHICAL STANDARDS

IsraAID has zero tolerance towards any acts of misconduct and Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA). The recruitment process will include all candidates' declarations and reference checks focused on misconduct and SEA.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES

IsraAID is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or disability status.

title: 26-120 Numerical Weather and Earth System Prediction Developer
description:
Job Description

The Cooperative Institute for Research in the Atmosphere (CIRA) at Colorado State University (CSU) seeks to fill a full-time research associate position designed to conduct collaborative research and development with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) located at the Global Systems Laboratory (GSL) in Boulder, CO. The individual in this position will work in the NOAA/OAR/GSL Earth Prediction Advancement Division (EPAD) Physics Branch.

The Cooperative Institute for Research in the Atmosphere at Colorado State University is a multi-million-dollar research organization located on CSU's Foothills Campus in Fort Collins, Colorado. CIRA is a cooperative institute that is also a research department within CSU's College of Engineering, in partnership with the Department of Atmospheric Science. Its vision is to conduct interdisciplinary research in the atmospheric sciences by entraining skills beyond the meteorological disciplines, exploiting advances in engineering and computer science, facilitating transitional activity between pure and applied research, leveraging both national and international resources and partnerships, and assisting the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, CSU, the State of Colorado, and the Nation through the application of our research to areas of societal benefit.


NOAA's Global Systems Laboratory is a federal science and research laboratory under NOAA’s Office of Oceanic and Atmospheric Research. GSL provides the National Weather Service (NWS) and the nation with environmental observation, prediction, computer, visualization, and information systems. These systems deliver data, forecasts, and predictions of weather, including severe weather events, within the next few minutes to weeks away. GSL is a leader in the applied research, directed development, and technology transfer of environmental data, models, products, and services that enhance environmental understanding with the outcome of supporting commerce, protecting life and property, and promoting a scientifically literate public.


Position Summary:

The individual in this position will be a technical lead for numerical weather and Earth system prediction model development in the context of NOAA’s Unified Forecast System (UFS) leveraging the Model for Prediction Across Scales (MPAS) atmospheric dynamical core. They will lead and assist the implementation of new and revised modeling capabilities, infrastructure, and workflows. A particular focus will be on porting modeling system codes to future NOAA research, development, and operational cloud-computing architectures. The individual in this position will also play a leading role in optimizing modeling system components to improve their computational efficiency while maintaining their scientific robustness and in managing the code bases for which GSL – and specifically Physics branch members – are the lead developers and maintainers. This position will report to the Ensemble Prediction Scientist.


Full Consideration Date: Monday, 9/28/2026, 11:59 pm (MT)


Essential Job Duties:

  • Be a technical lead for numerical weather and Earth system prediction system development, including leading and assisting with the technical implementation of new and revised modeling capabilities, infrastructure, and workflows.
  • Port modeling system codes in support of numerical weather and Earth system prediction systems to NOAA research, development, and operational cloud-computing architectures.
  • In collaboration with model, infrastructure, and physics parameterization developers, develop and implement code optimizations that reduce computational expense while maintaining scientific quality.
  • Lead the code management of the model, infrastructure, and physics parameterization codes for which GSL is the lead developing entity.

Conditions of Employment:

  • Initially, this position will require onsite presence. If project circumstances allow and with satisfactory performance, up to 2 days per week of telework may be allowed.
  • This full-time position requires a National Agency Check with Inquiries (NACI), tier 1 federal background check and a NOAA Common Access Card (CAC) ID badge for systems access. Therefore, only US citizens and lawful permanent residents with a physical USCIS “Green Card” are eligible.

Supervision:

The individual in this position will not supervise employees.


Required Qualifications:

NOTE: In the body of your resume, please specifically address all required qualifications when describing your work experience. A resume that fails to specifically address the qualifications of this position may not be further considered by the search committee.

  • A M.S. in Atmospheric Science, Computer Science, or related field and
  • At least two years of specialized technical experience developing, building infrastructure to support, and/or maintaining Earth system models.
  • At least three years of experience with Fortran and/or C++, Python, high-performance computing (cloud and/or on-premises), and Linux computing environments.
  • At least three years of experience with version control and the life cycle of complex software.
  • This position requires a National Agency Check with Inquiries (NACI), tier 1 federal background check and a NOAA Common Access Card (CAC) ID badge for systems access. Therefore, only US citizens and lawful permanent residents with a physical USCIS “Green Card” are eligible.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with state-of-the-art operational and/or research weather prediction systems.
  • Knowledge of cloud-computing environments for scientific applications.
  • Knowledge of best-practices for scientific code development, optimization, and management.
  • Experience communicating technical information, such as through technical reports, evaluations, and assessments, in ways that can be understood and acted upon by scientists and managers.

title: Tax Specialist
description:
At Dow, we believe in putting people first and we’re passionate about delivering integrity, respect and safety to our customers, our employees and the planet.

Our people are at the heart of our solutions. They reflect the communities we live in and the world where we do business. Their diversity is our strength. We’re a community of relentless problem solvers that offers the daily opportunity to contribute with your perspective, transform industries and shape the future. Our purpose is simple - to deliver a sustainable future for the world through science and collaboration. If you’re looking for a challenge and meaningful role, you’re in the right place.

About you and this role

The Tax Specialist will be part of the APAC Tax Team with primary responsibility for Philippines tax matters, while also providing broader APAC tax support across tax compliance, tax operations, tax accounting, tax audits and tax advisory. ​The position offers exposure to a broad range of direct and indirect tax matters across multiple jurisdictions.

This role requires tax technical expertise to analyze and interpret local tax legislation and provide practical business-focused advice. The position will work closely with internal stakeholders, including finance, business, legal, HR, external advisors, and tax authorities to ensure compliance with local tax regulations, manage tax risks, drive process improvements and support business growth across the region.

Key Responsibilities

Tax Compliance, Advisory and Operations

  • Manage corporate income tax, withholding tax, VAT, stamp duty, and other tax compliance obligations
  • Provide tax analysis and practical advice to the business
  • Research and interpret tax legislation, regulations, administrative guidance, and tax authority positions
  • Monitor legislative and tax policy developments, assess business impacts, and communicate key developments to stakeholders
  • Analyze tax implications of commercial transactions, supply chain changes, restructurings, legal entity rationalizations, and business initiatives
  • Prepare tax position papers, management presentations, and supporting documentation

Tax Accounting and Reporting

  • Support quarterly and annual tax provision processes under US GAAP
  • Prepare and review current and deferred tax calculations, tax account reconciliations, and supporting documentation
  • Assist with tax reporting, disclosures, uncertain tax position assessments, and tax risk evaluations
  • Develop and maintain tax procedures, documentation, and internal control frameworks

Tax Audit Management

  • Manage tax authority audits, reviews and investigations
  • Prepare and submit responses to tax authority enquiries and information requests
  • Respond to tax notices and assessments and file appeals where appropriate

Pillar Two and Transfer Pricing

  • Support Pillar Two compliance, reporting, data gathering, calculations, and implementation activities
  • Assist with transfer pricing monitoring, documentation and compliance

Process Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, and improve tax processes, controls, and governance
  • Support automation initiatives and implementation of tax technology solutions

Qualifications

  • Prefer 5–8 years of relevant tax experience in a multinational corporation, accounting firm, or equivalent environment
  • Strong technical knowledge of corporate income tax, indirect taxes (VAT/GST), withholding taxes, and international tax concepts
  • Demonstrated experience analyzing tax issues, interpreting legislation, and providing practical tax advice to business stakeholders
  • Experience supporting tax audits, appeals, tax authority enquiries, and controversy management

Your skills

  • Stakeholder Management & cross-functional collaboration: Work seamlessly with different functions and stakeholders with the ability to communicate technical tax issues in clear business language. Ability to lead responses to tax authorities and manage external advisors.
  • Operational Excellence & Attention to Detail: Ability to manage high-volume tax filings, ensure accuracy of tax reporting, meet deadlines, and maintain compliance with internal controls and regulatory requirements. Identify and resolve issues before submission.
  • Systems & Data Management: Experience working with SAP, tax portals, large datasets, Microsoft Excel and any other tools to support tax compliance, reporting, and process improvements.
  • Continuous Improvement Mindset: Demonstrated ability to streamline processes, improve controls, leverage automation, and enhance the efficiency and quality of tax operations.

Additional Notes

  • This role is based in Philippines, no relocation support will be provided.

Benefits – What Dow offers you

We invest in you.

Dow invests in total rewards programs to help you manage all aspects of you: your pay, your health, your life, your future, and your career. You bring your background, talent, and perspective to work every day. Dow rewards that commitment by investing in your total wellbeing.

Here are just a few highlights of what you would be offered as a Dow employee:

  • Equitable and market-competitive base pay and bonus opportunity across our global markets, along with locally relevant incentives.
  • Benefits and programs to support your physical, mental, financial, and social well-being, to help you get the care you need...when you need it.
  • Competitive retirement program that may include company-provided benefits, savings opportunities, financial planning, and educational resources to help you achieve your long term financial-goals.
    • Employee stock purchase programs (availability varies depending on location).
  • Student Debt Retirement Savings Match Program (U.S. only).
    • Dow will take the value of monthly student debt payments and apply them as if they are contributions to the Employees’ Savings Plan (401(k)), helping employees reach the Company match.
  • Robust medical and life insurance packages that offer a variety of coverage options to meet your individual needs. Travel insurance is also available in certain countries/locations.
  • Opportunities to learn and grow through training and mentoring, work experiences, community involvement and team building.
  • Workplace culture empowering role-based flexibility to maximize personal productivity and balance personal needs.
  • Competitive yearly vacation allowance.
  • Paid time off for new parents (birthing and non-birthing, including adoptive and foster parents).
  • Paid time off to care for family members who are sick or injured.
  • Paid time off to support volunteering and Employee Resource Group’s (ERG) participation.
  • Wellbeing Portal for all Dow employees, our one-stop shop to promote wellbeing, empowering employees to take ownership of their entire wellbeing journey.
  • On-site fitness facilities to help stay healthy and active (availability varies depending on location).
  • Employee discounts for online shopping, cinema tickets, gym memberships and more.
  • Additionally, some of our locations might offer:
    • Transportation allowance (availability varies depending on location)
    • Meal subsidiaries/vouchers (availability varies depending on location)
    • Carbon-neutral transportation incentives e.g. bike to work (availability varies depending on location)

Join our team, we can make a difference together.

About Dow
Dow (NYSE: DOW) is one of the world’s leading materials science companies, serving customers in high-growth markets such as packaging, infrastructure, mobility and consumer applications. Our global breadth, asset integration and scale, focused innovation, leading business positions and commitment to sustainability enable us to achieve profitable growth and help deliver a sustainable future. We operate manufacturing sites in 30 countries and employ approximately 36,000 people. Dow delivered sales of approximately $43 billion in 2024. References to Dow or the Company mean Dow Inc. and its subsidiaries. ​​​​Learn more about us and our ambition to be the most innovative, customer-centric, inclusive and sustainable materials science company in the world by visiting .

title: Project Assistant : Asia-Pacific Observatory
description:
Application Deadline : 18 September - 17:00 CET


Contract Duration

One-year fixed term with possibility of extension or renewal


Language Requirement

English


Location

Asean Countries


Background

The Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC) is an independent civil society organization headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, with a globally dispersed Secretariat working across 43 countries. Founded in 2013, GI-TOC brings together a global network of more than 810 independent experts and a team of over 150 staff dedicated to understanding and responding to organized crime. Through research, analysis, policy engagement and support to civil society actors, GI-TOC works to deepen understanding of organized crime and strengthen effective, rights-based responses.

The GI-TOC works to:


  • Identify, analyse and map criminal trends and patterns of regional instability, and their impact on illicit flows, governance, development, security, conflict and the rule of law.
  • Connect and support civil society actors working on organized crime and corruption, and on their links to instability and conflict.
  • Strengthen local monitoring and analysis of national, regional and international organized crime and insecurity trends.

Job Summary


Project Assistants work as part of multi-functional teams to deliver GI-TOC activities in an effective and efficient way, in line with GI-TOC policies, guidelines and norms. The project assistant will work under the direction of, and in close coordination with the Asia-Pacific Observatory Director, project leaders, the programme management team, and the other finance and core support teams.


Main Responsibilities and Specific Tasks


  • Work with the Head of the project to compile invoices for submission and ensure compliance with GI-TOC and donor guidelines.
  • Oversee procurement and contract management for the Observatory;
  • Liaise with relevant GI-TOC staff, experts and consultants to ensure submission of administrative documents and that these files are effectively stored
  • Ensure compliance with relevant regulations, policies and quality standards;
  • Support the delivery of programme activities and organize events (workshops, roundtables, webinars and networking activities etc.), including the preparation and dissemination of information and follow-up communications.
  • Provide administrative support to ensure the timely and efficient implementation of programme activities, including the arrangement of meetings when required.
  • Assist with travel arrangements (flights, accommodation) and DSA payments for participants of events organized;
  • Assist in the preparation of quarterly/annual progress and financial reports by acquiring and assembling the necessary information from relevant staff using reporting templates;
  • Support the preparation and coordination of the Observatory’s newsletter, event announcements, and other routine communications products.
  • Support the preparation of the PowerPoint development for outreach activities
  • Draft social media content and other communications materials
  • Maintain stakeholder and partner contact information, database and support routine relationship-management follow-up as directed
  • Track the Asia-Pacific Observatory team’s stakeholder engagement and communication activities
  • Support the development and regular updating of stakeholder maps
  • Serve as one of the focal points for the audit exercises of the project and provide the relevant documentation and actions to respond to auditors’ questions/requests.
  • Work closely with the other support teams – finance, programme management and HR.


Requisite Skills and Experience


The successful candidate will be able to demonstrate the following experience and skills:


  • Undergraduate degree in Management, Human Resources or Business
  • Extremely detail-oriented and responsible
  • Strong proficiency in using the Microsoft Office suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
  • Ability to work systematically and accurately according to strict deadlines and under pressure
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to undertake multiple tasks and activities in parallel
  • Independent, creative and highly motivated
  • Excellent communication skills (written and oral), collegiality and ability to work effectively in a multicultural environment and in a small team
  • At least 3 years’ experience in administrative and management support, preferably within international or foreign projects or organizations.
  • Fluency in spoken and written English. Command of more languages, particularly ASEAN languages would be considered an asset.

GI-TOC operates a flexible working environment and encourages staff to achieve a suitable work-life balance and supports professional development and learning.


Only short-listed candidates will be contacted.

Secondary Language(s) Job Description:

Specialist, Domain Enablement Analyst

The Opportunity

  • Based in Hyderabad, join a global healthcare biopharma company and be part of a 130- year legacy of success backed by ethical integrity, forward momentum, and an inspiring mission to achieve new milestones in global healthcare.
  • Be part of an organisation driven by digital technology and data-backed approaches that support a diversified portfolio of prescription medicines, vaccines, and animal health products.
  • Drive innovation and execution excellence. Be a part of a team with passion for using data, analytics, and insights to drive decision-making, and which creates custom software, allowing us to tackle some of the world's greatest health threats.

Our Technology Centers focus on creating a space where teams can come together to deliver business solutions that save and improve lives. An integral part of our companys’ IT operating model, Tech Centers are globally distributed locations where each IT division has employees to enable our digital transformation journey and drive business outcomes. These locations, in addition to the other sites, are essential to supporting our business and strategy.

A focused group of leaders in each Tech Center helps to ensure we can manage and improve each location, from investing in growth, success, and well-being of our people, to making sure colleagues from each IT division feel a sense of belonging to managing critical emergencies. And together, we must leverage the strength of our team to collaborate globally to optimize connections and share best practices across the Tech Centers.

Role Overview

  • Evaluate the business impact of product data quality, resolve product domain data issues and inquiries, curate business metadata for discoverability, and monitor adherence to business rules. Partner with governance and downstream teams to prioritize remediation and ensure product datasets are accurate, understandable, and fit for business use.

Key Responsibilities

  • Business Impact Monitoring and Prioritization
    • Assess how product domain quality affects key outcomes (e.g., time-to-market, fulfillment accuracy, margin, regulatory compliance, customer experience).
    • Quantify impact using clear metrics and scorecards; prioritize remediation based on business value, risk, and urgency.
    • Communicate findings, trade-offs, and recommendations via concise reports and dashboards to product, supply chain, commercial, and finance stakeholders.
  • Issue Resolution and Business Inquiries
    • Investigate and resolve disputes related to product domain definitions, ownership, lineage, and completeness/accuracy.
    • Manage intake and triage of ad hoc inquiries from business users; provide timely, well-documented responses with root-cause analysis and actions.
    • Drive cross-functional resolution through governance forums; maintain decision logs and track follow-ups to closure.
  • Business Metadata Cataloging and Curation
    • Curate and maintain business metadata for product datasets: context, definitions, descriptions, owners/stewards, usage notes, quality expectations, and authoritative sources.
    • Ensure datasets are discoverable and understandable in the enterprise catalog; keep entries current with versioning and change histories.
    • Align semantic definitions, classifications, and hierarchies with Product Master standards and enterprise taxonomies.
  • Business Rule Adherence and Governance Collaboration
    • Collaborate with governance/capability teams to define, monitor, and report on product business rule application (validation rules, identifier standards, hierarchy integrity, versioning/variant rules).
    • Track violations and exceptions; coordinate remediation plans, waivers, and timelines with accountable owners.
    • Provide periodic compliance summaries and escalate systemic issues through governance channels.
  • Measurement, Reporting, and Continuous Improvement
    • Create and maintain dashboards for product domain health (data quality scores, rule adherence, issue backlog, time-to-resolution, business impact realized).
    • Identify trends and recurring issues; recommend improvements to data capture, processes, and controls (e.g., DQ rules, validations, workflow changes).
    • Update playbooks, FAQs, and guidance to reduce future inquiries and improve self-service and literacy.

  • Bachelor of Science (or equivalent) in Data Science, Computer Science, Management Information Systems, IT, MBA, or an equivalent scientific/commercial discipline within the pharmaceutical industry.

  • Strong business acumen with a keen ability to understand how data can be leveraged to inform critical enterprise decisions and actions.
  • Proven ability to analyse and assess the value of data assets.
  • Proven potential to effectively collaborate with a broad range of internal and external stakeholders.
  • Intellectual curiosity and ability to identify innovative approaches to addressing data needs.
  • Excellent presentation, analytics, and communication skills, both written and oral, are required to synthesize key issues and communicate/persuade constituencies towards specific actions and initiatives.

  • Ability to learn and use new technologies
  • Ability to manage through complexity and ambiguity along with competing priorities.

  • Entrepreneurial spirit, motivated by uncovering new opportunities to add value to the organization

title: Undergraduate Internship Opportunity - Data Engineer
description:
VINCI GROUP – SPIECAPAG AUSTRALIA

VINCI is a world leader in concessions, energy and construction, operating in over 120 countries with a workforce of more than 294,000 employees. We are a Global Group with local company opportunities.

Spiecapag has been delivering large-scale pipeline infrastructure and drilling projects across Australia and the Asia Pacific region for more than 20 years. New projects and continuous growth mean we have a long‑term career opportunity with an industry leader.

About this role

Are you an engineering student with a strong interest in software development, data, technology and reporting?

We are inviting applications for an Undergraduate Internship Opportunity within our Data Team.

This Brisbane-based internship provides hands-on exposure to software development, data pipelines, reporting and analytics within a major construction and infrastructure organisation.

You’ll join us for 1 to 2 days per week for the remainder of the year, with the opportunity to increase to full-time hours over the summer break. For the right person, this internship could also be a valuable first step towards a graduate position next year, subject to performance and business needs.

Responsibilities

  • Software Development: Assist with developing, testing and improving internal tools, scripts and applications that support business and project delivery needs.
  • Data Pipelines: Support the design, maintenance and improvement of data workflows, including data collection, cleansing, transformation and integration activities.
  • Reporting & Analytics: Assist with preparing dashboards, reports and data summaries that provide clear, accurate and useful insights for internal stakeholders.
  • Process Improvement: Identify opportunities to automate routine tasks, improve reporting accuracy and streamline how teams access and use data.
  • Documentation & Data Quality: Maintain clear documentation, version control and data quality practices to support reliable and repeatable outputs.
  • Cross-functional Collaboration: Work closely with the data team, engineering, project delivery and corporate functions to understand business requirements and translate them into practical data and technology solutions.

To be considered, you’ll ideally bring

  • Current studies in Engineering, ideally with a focus on software, data, computer systems or a related discipline.
  • Strong interest in data and technology.
  • Strong interest in software development, data pipelines, reporting, analytics and emerging technology.
  • Analytical thinking, problem-solving skills and the ability to interpret and communicate data clearly.
  • Confidence using MS Office, particularly Excel; exposure to programming languages, databases, Power BI or similar reporting tools would be highly regarded.
  • High attention to detail, curiosity to learn and a proactive, team-first mindset.
  • Availability: 1 to 2 days per week for the remainder of the year, with potential to increase to full-time hours over the summer break.
  • Current Australian work rights.

What we offer

  • Practical, mentored experience within the data team supporting a major construction and infrastructure business.
  • A supportive learning culture backed by VINCI Group
  • Opportunities to develop technical, analytical and business-facing skills while contributing to real data, reporting and technology initiatives.

How to Apply

If you’re passionate about building a career in data, software and technology - and ready to learn by doing - we’d love to hear from you.

Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter outlining:

  • Why you’re interested in Spiecapag and joining the Data Team

title: NDT Inspector/Certified Welding Inspector (CWI)
description:
Summary

Ready to take your inspection expertise on the road?

We are seeking a highly skilled NDT Inspector / Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) to perform welding inspections, non-destructive testing (NDT), and quality assurance activities at customer sites and fabrication facilities. This position requires extensive travel (primarily regional with some overnight travel) and includes the use of a company-provided vehicle. The ideal candidate will ensure compliance with applicable codes, standards, customer specifications, and company quality requirements while representing the company professionally in the field.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) inspections using methods such as:
    • Visual Testing (VT)
    • Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)
    • Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)
    • Ultrasonic Testing (UT)
    • Radiographic Testing (RT) (preferred)
  • Conduct welding inspections in accordance with AWS, ASME, API, and customer specifications.
  • Travel to customer locations, fabrication shops, and field sites to perform inspections and quality assurance activities.
  • Safely operate a company-provided vehicle while traveling to assigned job sites.
  • Interpret Welding Procedure Specifications (WPS), Procedure Qualification Records (PQR), and Welder Performance Qualification (WPQ) records.
  • Review fabrication drawings, Inspection Test Plans (ITPs), and quality documentation.
  • Prepare detailed inspection reports and maintain accurate inspection records.
  • Identify weld and dimensional errors and recommend corrective actions.
  • Ensure compliance with company safety policies, customer requirements, and quality management systems.
  • Coordinate with production, engineering, quality personnel, customers, and third-party inspectors.
  • Participate in customer audits and third-party inspection

Required Qualifications

  • Current AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification (Preferred).
  • Level II certification in one or more NDT methods (VT, PT, MT, UT, RT) in accordance with ASNT SNT-TC-1A or NAS-410.
  • High school diploma or technical degree in Welding, Mechanical Engineering Technology, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in welding inspection and NDT.
  • Valid driver's license with a clean driving record.
  • Ability and willingness to travel 75–90% of the time, including overnight travel as required

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with ASME Section V, VIII, IX, API 1104, API 650, or AWS D1.1.
  • Knowledge of ISO 9001 quality systems.
  • Experience in heavy fabrication, structural steel, pressure vessels, or pipeline construction.
  • Strong understanding of welding processes including GTAW, GMAW, SMAW, FCAW, and SAW.

Skills

  • Strong knowledge of welding codes, specifications, and NDT standards.
  • Ability to read engineering drawings and welding symbols.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and inspection reporting software.
  • Ability to work independently in both field and shop environments.
  • Excellent time management and organizational skills with the ability to manage travel schedules and multiple inspection assignments

Certifications

  • AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) – Preferred
  • ASNT Level II (VT/MT/PT/UT/RT) – Preferred
  • Valid driver's license – Required

Who we are
At SMS group, our people are our greatest asset. We offer an entrepreneurial environment that promotes a culture of innovation, growth, and inclusion. We offer company events, activities, and opportunities to participate in charitable initiatives that benefit the communities where we are located.

What we offer
Competitive compensation, medical/dental/vision coverage, paid vacation, paid holiday time, 401k with a company match, training, a tuition reimbursement program and more!

SMS group is an industrial equipment manufacturer for the steel industry. We design, build, and service equipment and steel plants across the globe with a strong technical services/machine shop network in North America.

title: Regional Asset Protection Leader
description:
About us

KnitWell Group, a specialty retail operating company, comprises some of the most iconic brands in America – Ann Taylor, Chico's, Haven Well Within, Lane Bryant, LOFT, Soma, Talbots, White House Black Market. Individually, our brands are unique and strong. Together, we are powerful.


Our common thread is our commitment to create exceptional products, provide memorable experiences, and achieve superior results. Our associates are innovators who thrive through collaboration and are dedicated to excellence. At the heart of it all are the customers we serve. We are dedicated to creating fashion that not only looks good but also makes our customers feel good.


Regional Asset Protection Leader (RAPL) – NY Metro

About the role

The Regional Asset Protection Leader (RAPL) is primarily responsible for preventing financial loss caused by theft and fraud and for supporting safe store environments and operational excellence within the assigned region of NY Metro, New England and northern Mid-Atlantic (approximately 250 multi-brand stores). Regional Asset Protection Leaders are responsible for a multi-state region and are relationship based. They use data to strategically plan their time and conduct impactful store interactions.

The RAPL’s region consists of fashion specialty retail locations across multiple KnitWell Group brands (Ann Taylor, LOFT, Lane Bryant, Chico's, Soma, WHBM, Talbots & Haven Well Within). The RAPL leverages tools to minimize loss to the Company, including (but not limited to) identifying incidents of theft and fraud, reviewing business and exception reports, and partnering with field leaders to address risk while doing so with the least amount of organizational effort and expense.

The impact you can have

  • Serve as a primary contact for store teams and District Leaders during escalated in-store incidents, including critical and active incidents. Partner with stores to gather details, provide guidance, and support the KnitWell culture through strong emotional awareness.
  • Work in partnership with stores and District Leaders to share observations, provide development, and invest in teams, strategies, and goal commitments that address shrink and SKU variance performance, customer engagement, omni-channel execution, theft awareness, and other operational controllables.
  • Develop and manage asset protection initiatives and projects, in conjunction with Asset Protection leadership and field leadership, to deliver gross margin impact, reduce shrink, and improve processes and procedures through in-person, virtual, and phone-based support.
  • Partner with brand field leaders to connect store and business strategy with asset protection opportunities through effective communication and training to reduce shrink, margin erosion, and safety risks.
  • Independently and in partnership with field leadership, communicate asset protection awareness by teaching and managing implementation of policies and procedures through in-person, web-based, and phone-based methods.
  • Manage other strategic projects, as assigned, related to asset protection, shrink reduction, SKU variance, risk management, and safety across KnitWell Group stores and its distribution network.
  • Partner with the analytics team and Manager of Investigations to resolve losses attributed to omni-channel fraud or external theft. Actively investigate concerns related to suspicious losses to determine situational facts; conduct interviews with involved parties; resolve theft/fraud matters; and, when warranted, submit detailed written reports for each investigation in accordance with established guidelines.
  • Serve as a community liaison with law enforcement and other retail/asset protection partners to recover merchandise or cash, support case prosecution, and facilitate restitution when warranted.
  • Perform in-person and virtual store visits to ensure compliance with company policies, identify areas of loss, and execute strategies related to shrink, safety, physical security, and risk management.
  • Perform additional tasks, as needed, to meet business needs as determined by KnitWell Group leadership.

You’ll bring to the role

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred
  • Eight years of retail experience in asset protection or loss prevention preferred
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to develop these skill sets in others
  • Ability to interact and communicate with varying levels within the organizational structure
  • Ability to interact and communicate with varying levels within the organizational structure
  • Strong analytical skills sufficient to conduct research, determine relevance of information, and interpret meaning
  • Advanced investigation, interview, and interrogation skills preferred
  • Assist Risk Management and safety efforts, as needed
  • Intermediate computer proficiency with applications such as Microsoft Office applications
  • 50%+ Travel Requirement (covers all KWG Brands)
  • Required to work possible nights and weekends to respond to critical incidents, time sensitive investigations and address asset protection issues.
  • Extensive ability to manage administrative functions (time, expenses, budgets, scheduling, reporting, etc.)

Benefits

  • You will be eligible to receive a merchandise discount at select KnitWell Group brands, subject to each brand’s discount policies.
  • Support for your individual development plus opportunities for career mobility within our family of brands.
  • A culture of giving back – local volunteer opportunities, annual donation and volunteer match to eligible nonprofit organizations, and philanthropic activities to support our communities.*
  • Medical, dental, vision insurance & 401(K).*
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
  • Time off – paid time off & holidays.*
  • The target salary range for this role is: $100,000 – 115,000*

*Any job offer will consider factors such your qualifications, relevant experience, and skills. Eligibility of certain benefits and associate programs are subject to employment type and role.

title: Actuarial Analyst Intern

description:
Howden Re is the global reinsurance broker and risk, capital & strategic advisor focused on relentless innovation & superior analytics for top client service. ​ ​

About Role

Internship: Actuarial Analyst

Location: New York, NY/Edina, MN
Salary: Up to $30/hr (+ an additional $1 per passed exam) + overtime
Apply by: Friday 16th October

Introduction

You’ll join an energetic, quantitative, client-facing team that specializes in creating and executing P&C reserve solutions including creating client submissions, working on loss portfolio transfers, and capital modeling. The team is small but diverse with unlimited opportunity to learn, advance, and take on responsibility.

What you’ll be doing

Reinsurance is a complex world, the easiest way to think about it is that it’s insurance for the insurers. Working with our teams you’ll help insurance companies protect their futures, and the people they insure.

You’ll work across analytics, brokers, and other functions to identify and respond to client needs and develop additional opportunities related to products and services. Once you’ve collected the data, manipulated it in spreadsheets and other database applications, you’ll then prepare client-ready presentations to communicate analysis results to brokers and clients.

In addition you’ll also:

  • Understand reinsurance contracts and products (terminology, terms and conditions)

  • Manage workflow proactively and take initiative on internal projects to improve processes, products or services

  • Take ownership and responsibility for quality, accuracy and timely completion of analyses

  • Willingness to be part of Howden Re’s “Team First” culture and to offer help to others without prompting

Who we’re looking for

You’ll be actively pursuing a bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university with a 3.0 or higher graduating GPA; an advanced degree would be nice, but not a requirement.

You will:

  • Be actively pursuing a bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university with a GPA of 3.0 or higher

  • Be proficient in Excel, Word, and PowerPoint

  • Pay close attention to detail, because every small detail matters

  • Legally authorized to work in the US

Nice to have (but not expected)

  • Advanced degree

  • Experience in the (re)insurance industry

  • Completion of Actuarial exam(s) or be actively studying for an exam

Our Application process

Our application process is designed to help you show your potential, not to test what you already know!

Online application form: to make sure you’re eligible for the internship, and to upload a resume.

Pre-recorded video interview: You’ll record your answers to a few questions using your phone or laptop, giving you the chance to tell us more about yourself in your own time in a relaxed setting.

Assessment center: Our final stage is an assessment center, which will ideally be in-person, but may be virtual. You'll take part in some fun group activities and meet our team in a relaxed setting. This day is all about getting to know you better and for you to see what it's like to be part of Howden and experience our culture.

Different perspectives make us better

At Howden, we’re committed to fair opportunity, inclusive teams and a culture where everyone belongs. We value people of all backgrounds, identities and experiences. We make sure everyone has the chance to succeed. If you bring who you really are, we’ll help you to go further.

We believe in equal opportunities for all employees, regardless of race, religion, gender, age, sexual orientation or disability. And as a Disability Confident employer, we’re committed to removing barriers and supporting you to do your best work. If you need any adjustments during the application process or in the role, just let us know. We’re here to help.

What we offer:

A career that you define. We provide an environment where new ideas are encouraged and celebrated, where people who want to have a real hand in our success thrive. We want people who want to make a difference - not just in the workplace, but in the industry and in the wider community.

Working at Howden Re:

At Howden Re, we’re on a mission to do things differently. Our no silo approach, elite team, and clear focus on innovation and relentless execution means our clients are at the heart of all we do.

As a big 4 global reinsurance broker, we deliberately avoid the one-size-fits-all approach, committing to creating bespoke solutions that address the unique challenges of a modern and dynamic marketplace. Our team is empowered to drive progress, creating opportunities for career and personal development, unlocking new value for clients, fostering long-term partnerships, and using the collective power of Howden to change how the world sees risk and insurance.

When you join Howden Re, you become part of a vibrant and entrepreneurial workplace culture that prioritizes collaboration, ownership, and shared success. Here, your contributions will directly impact our mission to be the global partner of choice in reinsurance and strategic advisory.

Be a part of Howden Re's exciting journey. Together, we are shaping the future of reinsurance.
